model.rationale: The district's 12-point Democratic lean, Bronin's overwhelming fundraising advantage, and outside spending tilted in his favor leave Chai almost no visible path to an upset. Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee around 95%, and the open-seat nature of the race is the main source of residual uncertainty.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the race inside single digits, or a surge of Republican outside spending, would signal a genuine contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

Open seat: John B. Larson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Connecticut's 1st District is an open seat after longtime Democratic Representative John Larson lost renomination. Democrat Luke Bronin faces Republican Amy Chai, with Green candidate Mary Sanders also on the ballot. The district leans about 12 points Democratic, giving Bronin a strong structural base.

Money reinforces that edge. Bronin has raised about $3.7 million and benefits from roughly $1.35 million in outside support against about $516,000 in outside opposition, while Chai has raised only about $21,000 and had a few hundred dollars on hand. Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee around a 95 percent favorite. With no public polls of the general election, the outlook rests on district fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
